source:
Volunteer Arrival Experience: At this juncture, it is helpful to understand that the coffee stall volunteer journey begins with an arrival action. Arriving individuals should first undertake an apron retrieval step, with aprons being situated in the cupboard beneath the sink. This action facilitates readiness for participation.

Another dimension to bear in mind is that payment handling and drink preparation operate as distinct responsibility areas. A new volunteer does not undertake the payment responsibility area on their first shift. The shift leader will pair that person with a drink preparer, who will show them the order slips and the washing station.

Regarding the conclusion of participation, the volunteer should engage in an apron return action by placing the used apron in the laundry basket, which is located next to the cupboard. The shift leader should receive a verbal departure notification before the individual exits. A volunteer who feels unwell should tell the leader immediately and stop handling drinks.
objective: Reconstruct this orientation note as clear, friendly instructions for a new volunteer. Keep the actual steps, responsibilities, and illness instruction without adding procedures.

items.text:
Welcome to the coffee stall! When you arrive, take an apron from the cupboard beneath the sink.

On your first shift, you won't handle payments. The shift leader will pair you with a drink preparer, who will show you the order slips and the washing station.

When you finish, put your used apron in the laundry basket next to the cupboard. Tell the shift leader you're leaving before you go.

If you feel unwell, tell the leader immediately and stop handling drinks.
